name: Basal energy expenditure
seoTitle: Basal energy expenditure Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Basal energy expenditure: work out BEE (Results) from the height and the weight. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: BEE (Results) is what the Basal energy expenditure calculator works out, and it gets there from the height, the weight and the total Energy Expenditure. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Press Calculate for the answer; change a value and it steps off screen until you press again, so each edit can be judged on its own.

sections.title: How does the Basal energy expenditure calculator work?
sections.html:
The Basal energy expenditure calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports BEE (Results) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex, the activity and the stress); then you type in the height, the weight, the total Energy Expenditure (Results) and the total Energy Expenditure (Results).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Basal energy expenditure calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

BEE=-271 ÷ 40 × age (in years) + (5003 ÷ 1000) × height + (55 ÷ 4) × weight + 133 ÷ 2
Age (in years)=(925 ÷ 2338) × height + (9563 ÷ 4676) × weight − 250 ÷ 1169 × BEE + 163775 ÷ 1169
Temperature=total Energy Expenditure ÷ (activity × BEE × stress)
Temperature=total Energy Expenditure ÷ (activity × stress × BEE)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Time, opening in years
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Basal energy expenditure calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the height, the weight and the total Energy Expenditure — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Basal energy expenditure calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns BEE (Results), derived from the height, the weight and the total Energy Expenditure. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Basal energy expenditure calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the height, the weight and the total Energy Expenditure, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter age (in years) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Age (in years) opens in years and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (5 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Basal energy expenditure calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
